Reinforced-concrete cores and cross walls stabilize the low plan; roof lanterns use engineered curb frames and non-combustible glazing assemblies, with structure checked for seismic loads and thermal movement.
projects.constructionLogic: Build the compact low-rise wings on surveyed foundations with damp-proof courses, then install stone masonry, insulated flat roof decks and lantern curbs. Form roof falls to primary drains plus visible emergency overflows, use membrane upstands at parapets and lanterns, and detail water courts as independent waterproofed basins with recirculation plant, accessible balance tanks, non-slip edges and isolation joints from the building.
projects.environmentalResponse: Use thick shaded walls, recessed openings and carefully oriented roof lanterns to provide diffuse daylight without glare or excessive solar gain; favor cross-ventilation in dry seasons and efficient dehumidification for wet rooms. Shade both courts with drought-adapted trees, recirculate water and control evaporation, harvest roof runoff for non-potable use, and direct stormwater to planted swales without overwatering the plateau landscape.
